other.body:
A web session now brings its Artifact and GitHub level at its start: after the board's pull, one command loads the Artifact, takes what GitHub has that the Artifact lacks, sends GitHub what only the Artifact has, and prints one line saying both. A post changed on both sides since the last time is never overwritten without a word: the newer copy shows, and the other is kept whole in a comment under the post. On this very board it found CL44 shown "in progress" on the Artifact while GitHub had it complete with its review, and took GitHub's copy.

### What runs at a web session's start
1. `web_takeover.py` (turn 1): for an Artifact board it no longer runs the git-only reconcile (that one put GitHub's copies into the local board before the Artifact's, and the posts only GitHub had were then marked "never in the Artifact" and never sent: the bug). It prints the board's pull instead.
2. The pull's last line, on the web, now says `kit.py artifact reconcile` instead of `artifact load`; so does resume's STALE line the first time on the web; the session-start hook's WEB line names it too.
3. `kit.py artifact reconcile`: runs `artifact load`, reads origin/board-mirror, compares post by post and comment by comment, writes the board here, commits and pushes board-mirror (what it lacks, plus `board/artifact-reconciled.json`, the record of what both sides held), then builds the Artifact batches (`artifact push`) and prints them under the one line.

### How a document is decided
- in one side only: it goes to the other (GitHub only: here, then a create in the Artifact batch; Artifact only: written to board-mirror)
- equal: nothing
- different, and the record says one side still holds what both had: the side that changed wins, whatever the dates say
- different, and both changed since the record: the newer copy (its `updated_at`, else `created_at`, else the git commit time) shows on the board and in git; the other is kept whole in a comment `conflict-<hash>` under the post (`kind: conflict`, `conflict.other` holds the full copy, the text quotes it); the comment id is fixed, so a rerun never doubles it
- different, no record yet (the first run): the newer copy wins, counted, no comment (before the first record there is nothing to tell "changed on both sides" from "an older copy")
- the record of a document is moved forward only when the Artifact already holds the final copy; one still in an unsent batch keeps its old record, so a batch never sent cannot make the next run take the Artifact's stale copy over GitHub's

### Local sessions
`artifact reconcile` in a local session prints that it does not run there (a computer reconciles its own board with `kit.py reconcile`) and changes nothing. A review, a check or KIT_NO_BOARD_PUSH never writes the git copy.

### Files
- `scripts/kit.py` (and its installed copy `.kit/kit.py`): `artifact_reconcile`, `artifact_reconcile_line`, the `reconcile` action of `kit.py artifact`, the pull and STALE texts on the web, the commands list
- `kit/web_takeover.py` (and `.kit/`): an Artifact board's start prints the pull and the reconcile, no git-only reconcile first
- `kit/hooks/kit_session_start.py` (and `.kit/`): the WEB line names it
- `tests/test_cl45_artifact_reconcile.py`: the test (item 4)

A Claude Code web session reconciles its Artifact with GitHub at its start, the same way `board` reconciles the local board with GitHub on a computer: each post and comment, the newer copy wins, nothing lost on either side.

Today the pieces exist (`kit.py artifact pull`, `load`, `kit.py reconcile` against board-mirror, `artifact push`), but nothing runs them together, so a web session found its Artifact missing the posts made on the computer (the memory train's M5 to M8, the runners train) and called the git copy out of date.

1. `kit.py artifact reconcile`: pull and load the Artifact, reconcile with origin/board-mirror (newer wins, per document), push what changed both ways (the Artifact batch, and board-mirror), and print one line: what came from GitHub, what went to it.
2. It runs by itself at a web session's start (the web's session-start hook or resume on the web), never in a local session (a local session reconciles its own board).
3. A document changed on both sides since the last reconcile is never overwritten silently: both versions are kept and the board shows the conflict.
4. A test with an Artifact copy and a board-mirror that each hold a post the other lacks, and one changed on both.
5. Attached files travel with their posts, every way: `kit.py reconcile` (local board and GitHub) and the Artifact reconcile bring in board/blobs/* the other side has, not only posts and comments. On 2026-11-26 R1's 4 files (patch, adapter, tests, review guide) were on board-mirror but missing from the local board (its page would 404 them) until copied by hand.
